free_tier.stated: No free tier at any of the four. DediRock Yearly Promo VPS Saver USD 10.88/year for 10 GB SSD, 1 GB RAM, 1 vCPU, 1 TB bandwidth, 1 IPv4; VolpaByte EUR 3.49 a month for the 4 GB rung, with a free test server sold alongside; Datalix EUR 2.45 a month for the cheapest in-stock rung.
free_tier.notes: Four hosts, four prices, none of them free. The prices are carried here from compute/racknerd, compute/dedirock, compute/volpabyte-ryzen-kvm-8gb and compute/datalix, which read the vendor pages on 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-24. This record exists for the ASN field, not the price, so the price is quoted only to establish that the four are buyable.

per_object_cap.notes: The unit of this record is an ASN, which is a routing identity, not a stored object. There is no largest-single-object question to answer.

retention.stated: not applicable: an address, not an object
retention.notes: An address is held for as long as the machine holding it is paid for. The nearest real retention fact is Datalix's term rule, recorded in limits[]: the server is locked at the end of the prepaid term and deleted 5 days later, so the address goes with it.

egress.terms: The traffic position differs per host and none of the four quotes an ASN in it. Datalix states 10 TB a month on a 1 Gbit uplink and, on exhaustion, quotes 'wird die Geschwindigkeit Ihres Servers auf 10 MB/s (80Mbit/s) begrenzt', with more traffic buyable. RackNerd's specials page lists 3000 GB a month on a 1 Gbps port. DediRock's card states 1 TB of bandwidth and prints no period and no overage price. VolpaByte's plan page lists a 1 Gbit/s connection and no traffic figure at all; its homepage's older copy said 'unlimited traffic'.
egress.free_allowance: 10 TB a month (Datalix), 3000 GB a month (RackNerd), 1 TB with no period printed (DediRock), not stated (VolpaByte)

interface_detail: A VPS is reached by SSH into a root shell, plus the vendor's web control panel: RackNerd, DediRock and Datalix sell KVM guests with root; VolpaByte sells KVM with a WHMCS client area. The egress leaves from the guest's own address, so a SOCKS5 or HTTP proxy is something a user runs on the guest, not a protocol the host sells.
tooling: Any SSH client, plus whatever proxy a user runs on the guest: a SOCKS5 or HTTP listener, an SSH -D tunnel, or a WireGuard server if the host allows it. No host in this set sells a proxy endpoint or a proxy wrapper, and no wrapper existing is not a rejection: the resource is a machine with a routable address, which is what a proxy needs.

limits_note: The constraint this record is actually about names no kind in the vocabulary: the ASN is not a property of the host. DediRock holds none and its test addresses sit in AS36352 and AS40676; VolpaByte's Frankfurt location exits from AS24940 Hetzner; Datalix's own AS218841 announces zero prefixes and its traffic leaves via AS58087. A field that names one ASN per host therefore cannot describe any of the four, and the same host answers differently depending on which location was bought.
binding_note: the others are 10 TB a month and 3000 GB a month. What fails first is not a quota but the record shape: an ASN is per location and sometimes not the host's at all, so a single-ASN field per host is wrong before any traffic is sent.

identity_cost.detail: The set does not share one gate, and the weakest documented is an email address. Datalix's order page shows the sign-up fields 'Nutzername', 'E-Mail', 'Passwort' and 'Sprache', with no phone field and no identity document; payment is a prepaid account balance. VolpaByte's registration form asks for name, email, phone with a full country selector and address, and its payment step could not be read because the order store was empty: unverified rather than none. RackNerd's signup requirement and DediRock's were not read in their lanes and are recorded there as unverified and not read, so this record does not claim a gate for them.

reliability_note: The exit's reputation belongs to whichever upstream announces the address, not to the host named on the invoice: RackNerd's addresses resolve to HostPapa/ColoCrossing, Multacom, Mamut Rahal and Psychz space, and Datalix's own AS218841 announces nothing while its front end sits in Florian Kolb's AS58087. A host that changes upstream changes the ASN under an unchanged product.
confidence_note: The ASN half of the verdict is measured: every ASN in this record was resolved with RIPEstat on 2026-10-24, and the zero-prefix answer for AS218841 was read from as-overview and announced-prefixes, not from a vendor claim.

evidence.proved: RackNerd's Los Angeles DC-02 test address 204.13.154.3 sits in 204.13.152.0/22, announced by AS35916 MULTA-ASN1 - MULTACOM CORPORATION. The address is not in a RackNerd ASN because RackNerd holds none.
RackNerd's Los Angeles DC-05 test address 5.181.135.8 sits in 5.181.135.0/24, announced by AS198566 MAMUTRAHAL - MAMUT RAHAL SOFTWARE FZCO. A second RackNerd location, a second unrelated ASN.
DediRock's New York test address 199.188.100.133 sits in 199.188.100.0/24, announced by AS36352 AS-COLOCROSSING - HostPapa.
DediRock's Los Angeles test address 198.37.127.161 sits in 198.37.127.0/24, announced by AS40676 - Psychz Networks. Two DediRock locations, two ASNs, neither of them DediRock's.
AS218841's holder is 'DatalixGmbH Datalix GmbH' and as-overview returns announced: false, so the host owns an ASN that originates nothing.
AS218841 announces zero prefixes, v4 and v6 alike. This is the zero in the headline and it is a count, not an inference from the absent holder page.

datalix.de's A record 194.15.36.245 sits in 194.15.36.0/24, announced by AS58087 FlorianKolb Florian Kolb. This is the vendor's own front end, not a guest's egress path, so it corroborates the AS58087 attribution without proving where a bought server's traffic leaves.

volpabyte.net and its status, lg and speedtest subdomains all resolve to 179.61.251.70, in 179.61.251.0/24 announced by AS211301 UNESTY Collin Schneeweiss trading as Unesty Company. This does not reproduce AS24940 for VolpaByte and is recorded as a contradiction, not as confirmation.

Ten further RackNerd looking-glass test addresses (192.3.81.8, 192.3.253.2, 192.3.254.158, 192.210.207.88, 198.23.228.15, 198.23.249.100, 107.173.164.160, 107.174.51.158, 167.160.186.8, 23.94.101.88) all resolve to AS36352 HostPapa/ColoCrossing, a fourth ASN in RackNerd's published set and the one carrying most of its locations.

AS24940's holder is HETZNER-AS Hetzner Online GmbH with 96 announced prefixes, so the ASN the commission attributes to VolpaByte's Frankfurt location exists and is a hosting network. The holder is established; the attribution of VolpaByte's traffic to it is not.

DediRock's Yearly Promo VPS Saver at USD 10.88 a year with 1 TB of bandwidth on a 1 Gbps connection, read from the vendor page by the compute lane on 2026-10-22 and carried here through compute/dedirock.

price_per_tb_month: no per-TB figure is published by any of the four; entry prices are USD 21.99/year (RackNerd), USD 10.88/year (DediRock), EUR 3.49/month (VolpaByte) and EUR 2.45/month (Datalix)
notes: This record exists because the obvious shape for an ASN field is wrong. Candidates for how a host's ASN could be established, and what testing each produced: (1) take the host's own claim or its marketing page, which is refuted for all four because none of the four pages read names an ASN at all; (2) look up an ASN registered to the host's name, which returned nothing for RackNerd, DediRock and VolpaByte in RIPEstat searchcomplete and a 404 in ARIN RDAP entity search, and returned AS218841 for Datalix with zero announced prefixes; (3) resolve each host's published test address and read the origin ASN, which is the method that produced every ASN here and the only one that answers the question. The third is what this record carries. It also shows the field is not one value per host but one per location: RackNerd's published test addresses span AS35916, AS198566, AS40676 and AS36352, DediRock's span AS36352 and AS40676, and Datalix's own ASN carries none of its traffic. Any future record that writes one ASN for a multi-location host is a defect, and this record is the evidence for that rule. Two things are stated with less certainty than the rest. Second, VolpaByte: the commission says its Frankfurt location exits from AS24940 Hetzner, and three published YABS runs of VolpaByte Frankfurt guests plus the vendor's own hostnames all return AS211301 Unesty Company, which contradicts it; The structural finding survives either answer, because AS211301 is no more VolpaByte's ASN than AS24940 is. five records mention an ASN inside tooling or evidence prose and none of those is a field. This record does not correct a wrong ASN in compute/racknerd, dedirock.json, volpabyte-ryzen-kvm-8gb.json or datalix.json, because those files assert no ASN

extras.one_asn_per_host_is_a_defect: Any record that writes a single ASN for a multi-location host is wrong. The ASN is per location and sometimes not the host's at all: Datalix owns AS218841 and announces nothing from it, and RackNerd owns no ASN while its addresses sit in four other operators' networks.
